page: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-16g-4vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel x86_64 processor offering 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core with hyper-threading. The system features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU representing a 0.25 share of the physical card, which delivers 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided via an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear division between CPU-bound and GPU-assisted workloads. Single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1778.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1458.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2647.0 and a passmark CPU score of 3681.75. Memory bandwidth is also weak, measuring 28.99 GB/sec for large block reads. Conversely, the bundled GPU excels at specific tasks, demonstrating top-tier prompt processing speeds for LLM inference, reaching 8765.82 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and 308.92 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds are strong for the 135M model at 296.05 tokens/sec but drop to a weak 7.83 tokens/sec for the 7B model.

This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU allocation. Users gain access to NVIDIA Ampere architecture and dedicated VRAM without the expense of provisioning a full GPU. However, the trade-off is limited CPU and memory bandwidth performance, making it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded CPU processing or high-throughput database operations. It is best suited for small-scale LLM inference, lightweight machine learning model deployment, GPU-based development and testing, and basic parallel processing tasks that fit within the 4 GB VRAM limit.
